author: Rahul kp
topic: Movement vs Shift of Demand Curve
title: Movement vs Shift
hook: price moves it, or something else?
simple_words: Own price changes: slide along the same curve. Any other factor changes: the whole curve moves.

definitions.meaning: Change in quantity demanded caused only by a change in the good's own price, other factors constant. Called extension or contraction.
Change in demand at every price, caused by a change in a factor other than own price. Called increase or decrease in demand.

key_points: Own price is the ==only cause== of a movement along the curve.
Income, tastes, related goods' prices, expectations and number of buyers cause a ==shift==.
Price fall gives extension; price rise gives contraction of demand.
!!Do not say 'increase in demand' when only own price has fallen!!

insight.text: Check the cause first: only own price means movement; any other factor means shift.

memory_trick.explanation: Picture a child on a slide: own Price makes you slide along the curve. Any Other factor shifts the whole slide to a new place.

steps: Is it the good's own price?
Yes: move along the same curve
exam_tip: In MCQs, underline the changed factor. Own price means extension or contraction; anything else means increase or decrease in demand.

doubt.question: If income rises, does demand always shift right?
doubt.answer: No. For a normal good it shifts right. For an inferior good, higher income shifts the curve left.

mistakes.wrong: Price of the good falls, so 'demand increases'
mistakes.right: Own price fall causes extension of demand, a movement down along the same curve.

mistakes.wrong: Income change shown as a movement along the curve
mistakes.right: Income change shifts the whole demand curve.

mistakes.wrong: Rise in price of a substitute causes contraction of demand for the good
mistakes.right: It shifts the demand curve of the good to the right (increase in demand).

check_notes: Checker 1: Step 5 ('Name it: extension or increase') is incomplete. It lists only two of the four terms, which could suggest that a movement is always an extension and a shift is always an increase. Correct version: 'Name it: extension/contraction for a movement, increase/decrease in demand for a shift.'
Checker 1: Key point 4 has no full stop at the end. Correct version: 'Do not say 'increase in demand' when only own price has fallen.' It could also add: 'call it extension of demand.'
Checker 1: Table row 5 (Ceteris paribus: Holds / Does not hold) is correct but could be clearer. Suggested wording: 'Other factors constant / A factor other than own price changes.'
